input.query: SELECT metric, service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name pod, attr_k8s_node_name node, CAST(floor(epoch(time)/60) AS BIGINT) AS minute, round(avg(value),4) v, count(*) n FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE metric IN ('container.cpu.usage','container.memory.working_set','k8s.pod.cpu.usage') AND (service_name='search' OR service_name IS NULL OR service_name='' OR service_name='geo') GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5 ORDER BY 1,2,5

content.text: Search's pod CPU is pinned at about 2.8 cores from the start of the incident window, while its own span latency stays flat. I'll compare the cumulative metrics per service to see whether other services (memcached, mongodb, network) show a similar shift.

input.query: SELECT metric, service_name, count(*) n_abn_norm, round(avg(CASE WHEN src='a' THEN value END),2) abn_avg, round(avg(CASE WHEN src='n' THEN value END),2) norm_avg, round(max(CASE WHEN src='a' THEN value END),2) abn_max, round(max(CASE WHEN src='n' THEN value END),2) norm_max FROM (SELECT 'a' src, * FROM abnormal_metrics_sum UNION ALL SELECT 'n', * FROM normal_metrics_sum) WHERE metric IN ('container.cpu.time','k8s.pod.cpu.time','k8s.pod.network.errors') GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1,2

content.text: Search is the only service whose CPU time changed materially (mean 454 vs 80 per series, peak 918 vs 81). Before deciding whether that reaches users, I'll check status codes and HTTP response codes, which I haven't inspected yet.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' p, attr_status_code sc, attr_http_response_status_code code, count(*) n FROM abnormal_traces GROUP BY 1,2,3 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', attr_status_code, attr_http_response_status_code, count(*) FROM normal_traces GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 1,2,3

content.text: No error codes anywhere, so the fault doesn't show as failures in traces. I'll check the span-metric call counters against the trace counts, which could reveal dropped or sampled requests.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' p, service_name, count(*) n_series, round(sum(value),0) total, min(value) mn, max(value) mx FROM abnormal_metrics_sum WHERE metric='traces.span.metrics.calls' GROUP BY 1,2 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', service_name, count(*), round(sum(value),0), min(value), max(value) FROM normal_metrics_sum WHERE metric='traces.span.metrics.calls' GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 2,1

content.text: Those counters are cumulative and the series counts differ, so they don't give a clean comparison. Next I'll compute own time (span duration minus child durations) for each server span, to see whether any service's internal work grew.

input.query: WITH a AS (SELECT 'abn' p, * FROM abnormal_traces UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', * FROM normal_traces), c AS (SELECT p, parent_span_id, sum(duration) cd FROM a GROUP BY 1,2), s AS (SELECT s.p, s.service_name, s.span_name, s.attr_span_kind k, s.duration - coalesce(c.cd,0) own FROM a s LEFT JOIN c ON c.p=s.p AND c.parent_span_id=s.span_id WHERE s.attr_span_kind='Server') SELECT service_name, span_name, round(quantile_cont(own filter (WHERE p='abn'),0.5)/1e6,3) abn_own_p50, round(quantile_cont(own filter (WHERE p='norm'),0.5)/1e6,3) norm_own_p50, round(quantile_cont(own filter (WHERE p='abn'),0.95)/1e6,3) abn_own_p95, round(quantile_cont(own filter (WHERE p='norm'),0.95)/1e6,3) norm_own_p95, count(*) n FROM s GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1,2

WITH a AS (SELECT 'abn' p, * FROM abnormal_traces UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', * FROM normal_traces), c AS (SELECT p, parent_span_id, sum(duration) cd FROM a GROUP BY 1,2), s AS (SELECT s.p, s.service_name, s.span_name, s.duration - coalesce(c.cd,0) own FROM a s LEFT JOIN c ON c.p=s.p AND c.parent_span_id=s.span_id WHERE s.attr_span_kind='Server') SELECT service_name, span_name, p, count(*) n, round(quantile_cont(own,0.5)/1e6,3) own_p50, round(quantile_cont(own,0.95)/1e6,3) own_p95 FROM s GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 1,2,3

content.text: Own-time comparisons show no consistent shift in service internals (the reservation and rate own-time differences look like span-structure artifacts). The one clear resource anomaly is search's container CPU. I'll check the node-level CPU view to tell container saturation from a single-process problem.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' p, metric, service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name pod, round(avg(value),3) v FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE metric IN ('k8s.pod.cpu.node.utilization','k8s.pod.cpu.usage') AND service_name IN ('search','rate','frontend','reservation') GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', metric, service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name, round(avg(value),3) FROM normal_metrics WHERE metric IN ('k8s.pod.cpu.node.utilization','k8s.pod.cpu.usage') AND service_name IN ('search','rate','frontend','reservation') GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 ORDER BY 2,3,1
